ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Approximately 0.35:0.65 ratio of high-intensity (white) to low-intensity (black) pixels across the visible ventral fluke surface.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Two primary high-contrast contiguous white regions are localized at the distal lateral extremities of both lobes. The left lobe patch is concentrated along the trailing tip. The right lobe patch is more expansive, extending from the tip toward the midline with highly irregular, mottled interior boundaries and isolated dark spots within the white field.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Central V-shaped depression with an approximate internal angle of 52 degrees; the notch depth creates a distinct bisection of the fluke lobes.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency irregular serrations are present along the entire trailing edge boundary. Pixel-amplitude of these variations ranges from 5 to 15 pixels, with the most acute and frequent peaks located on the lateral thirds of both lobes.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Trailing edges exhibit a convex mathematical curve from the notch to the tips, while the overall fluke orientation shows an upward-flaring parabolic sweep.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Small circular high-contrast white pixel clusters (2-5 pixel diameter) are visible near the trailing edge of the left lobe and within the white pigment field of the right lobe tip, suggestive of colonial barnacle attachment sites.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Two prominent, unaligned diagonal white linear scars are detected on the right lobe; the primary mark extends from the central black region toward the lateral tip, with a shorter parallel mark located medially.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: A significant diagonal linear scar on the right lobe and several small V-shaped tissue indentations (nicks) along the trailing edge of the left lobe.
